items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: I wanted to take my wife, and Gertrude said she couldn't go and leave the children.

ctx.x: Oh, yes. That's beautiful. I read some of these reports and I just wanted you to say it as a matter of record.

You know, it came -- when he graduated high school it was the summer I went to the Soviet Union with Benny Goodman, 1962. And I didn't really want to go and I was putting up all kinds of obstacles, asking a ridiculous price and then I said I wanted to take my wife, and Gertrude said she couldn't go and leave the children. So I said, well, I want to take my son. Benny said, 'Well, I'll give him a job in the band,' which later he didn't but I took him anyhow. Which was difficult, to take a member of the family to…

So I took him along with me and when he went to college he was going to be a chemist. And he thought about it and decided he wanted to study Russian because he wanted to go in the State Department. And he talked to the people in the Embassy in Moscow and he said, these people are hopeless, you know. They want war with the Soviet Union and everything else. He said, I feel I should do something for the government so I think I'll study Russian and go into the diplomatic service. But later he felt he'd rather be a…
